scenario.name: Docker Official Security, CISA & MITRE — Exposed Docker Daemon TCP Port 2375 API & Host Bind-Mount Audit
scenario.overview: Imagine a massive robotic warehouse whose master crane control console is wired onto an open hallway radio channel with no padlock or badge check. An outsider spots the open radio channel, orders the crane to drop a wide-open glass booth with a direct door into the warehouse main vault, and steps through that doorway to plant permanent maintenance schedules on the warehouse master wall. In this scenario (T1613, Docker Official Security, CISA & MITRE, Exposed Docker Daemon TCP Port 2375 API & Host Bind-Mount Audit), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: unauthenticated Docker Engine REST API, then pOST /containers/create, then host Root Filesystem chroot. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Unauthenticated Docker Engine REST API, then POST /containers/create, then Host Root Filesystem chroot, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates process, authentication, and network telemetry for T1613 across the documented kill chain.

specs.value: Never bind dockerd to unencrypted TCP port 2375 (-H tcp://0.0.0.0:2375); bind strictly to unix:///var/run/docker.sock or enforce mutual TLS (--tlsverify) on TCP port 2376 with host firewall restrictions.

stages.title: Stage 1: Unauthenticated Docker Engine REST API Discovery (GET /v1.43/version & /containers/json)
stages.subtitle: Discovery (T1613 - Container and Resource Discovery)
stages.description: Scanning the warehouse hallways for open control panels, the intruder tunes into an unlocked crane radio channel that immediately replies with the crane exact model number and a complete inventory of every cargo box currently running on the floor. When dockerd is started with -H tcp://0.0.0.0:2375 without TLS (--tlsverify), any network client can reach the REST API over cleartext HTTP. The client queries GET /version and GET /containers/json to fingerprint the host kernel and running workloads (logged in Linux Audit Event 200 with DaemonSocket=tcp://0.0.0.0:2375 , Unencrypted HTTP, RestEndpoint=GET /v1.43/version, RemoteClient=198.51.100.55:49210 so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes ss -tulpn | grep 2375 (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ss -tulpn | grep 2375 via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the exact arguments so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1613 during "Unauthenticated Docker Engine REST API Discovery , GET /v1.43/version & /containers/json" , When dockerd is started with -H tcp://0 while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact journalctl -u docker.service | grep "/containers/json" runs (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , journalctl -u docker.service | grep "/containers/json" configuring pod security co so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1613 during "Unauthenticated Docker Engine REST API Discovery , GET /v1.43/version & /containers/json" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). stages.title: Stage 2: POST /containers/create with HostConfig.Binds ["/:/hostfs"] & Privileged=true
stages.subtitle: Execution (T1610 - Deploy Container)
stages.description: Speaking directly into the unlocked crane console, the intruder orders the crane to lower a lightweight utility box onto the floor with all safety bars removed and its entire back wall hinged directly onto the warehouse master storage room. The remote client sends POST /v1.43/containers/create specifying an Alpine image, HostConfig.Privileged=true, and HostConfig.Binds=["/:/hostfs:rw"], followed by POST /containers/<id>/start (logged in Linux Audit Event 201 with ApiAction=POST /v1.43/containers/create, HostBindMount=/:/hostfs:rw, PrivilegedFlag=true so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes docker inspect <container_id> --format "{{json .HostConfig.Binds}} Privileged={{.HostConfig.Privileged}}" (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , docker inspect <container_id> --format "{{json .HostConfig.Binds}} Privileged={{.H so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1610 during "POST /containers/create with HostConfig.Binds ["/:/hostfs"] & Privileged=true" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). Next, the follow-up artifact ausearch -k docker_daemon_api -i runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ausearch -k docker_daemon_api -i via System / Runtime Execution Interface, passing the exact so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1610 during "POST /containers/create with HostConfig.Binds ["/:/hostfs"] & Privileged=true" , The remote client sends POST /v1.43/containers/create specifying an Alpine image, HostConfig.Privileged=true, and HostConfig.Binds=["/:/hostfs:rw"], followed by POST /containers/<id>/start while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ POST /v1.43/containers/create (Privileged=true, Binds=["/:/hostfs:rw"]) / ⇠#2 ACK 201) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 dockerd Daemon (-H tcp://0.0.0.0:2375)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Linux Host Root Filesystem (/)).

keySpecs.value: Deploy OPA Gatekeeper / Docker Authorization Plugins (AuthZ) and Falco runtime rules that alert on and block any container started with Privileged=true or a host root (/) bind mount.

stages.title: Stage 3: Host Root Filesystem chroot (/hostfs) & Cron/SSH Persistence Audit
stages.subtitle: Escape to Host (T1611 - Escape to Host)
stages.description: Once the utility box lands on the floor, the intruder steps through the hinged back wall straight onto the warehouse master floor, adding their own spare front-door key and repeating daily work order directly onto the building permanent host schedules. Inside the started container, the entrypoint executes chroot /hostfs /bin/sh to operate directly inside the host root filesystem as UID 0, modifying /etc/crontab or /root/.ssh/authorized_keys, which Linux auditd and Falco eBPF sensors capture (logged in Linux Audit Event 161 with Syscall=sys_chroot , 161, TargetRootPath=/hostfs , Host Root /, FalcoAlert=Launch Privileged Container & Host Root Mount so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes ausearch -f /etc/crontab -i (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , ausearch -f /etc/crontab -i via crontab, passing the exact arguments, target paths, and prot so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1611 during "Host Root Filesystem chroot , /hostfs & Cron/SSH Persistence Audit" , Inside the started container, the entrypoint executes chroot /hostfs /bin/sh to operate directly inside the host root filesystem as UID 0, modifying /etc/crontab or /root/ while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact docker ps --no-trunc --filter "status=running" runs (which executes a Kubernetes API request or container runtime command , docker ps --no-trunc --filter "status=running" configuring pod security contexts so that breaks out of container cgroup/namespace isolation , T1611 during "Host Root Filesystem chroot , /hostfs & Cron/SSH Persistence Audit" to gain unrestricted root execution on the underlying Kubernetes worker node and access host credentials , kubelet / systemd). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ chroot /hostfs /bin/sh -c "cat /etc/shadow" / ⇠#3 ACK 161) from Node ③ (#3 dockerd Daemon (-H tcp://0.0.0.0:2375)) to Node ④ (#4 Privileged Container (/:/hostfs)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Linux Host Root Filesystem (/)).

keySpecs.value: Enable user namespaces (--userns-remap=default in /etc/docker/daemon.json) so container UID 0 maps to an unprivileged high UID on the host, and monitor chroot syscalls inside container cgroups.
